transcript.text: I need to share an important finding from my latest reconciliation. While going through a late-produced onboarding export against the user-agreement database, I confirmed that exactly 312 of the 480 putative class members have executed agreements containing an arbitration provision. The remaining 168 do not have arbitration provisions. I have not yet incorporated this reconciliation into the arbitration analysis, but this split is critical for our strategy — we can only compel arbitration for 312 of the 480 putative class members, and the other 168 would remain in the litigation absent some other basis.

transcript.text: To add a bit more context on the discovery front: the late-produced onboarding export was something we only recently received, so I'd recommend we update the arbitration analysis promptly to reflect the 312/168 split before we make any filings. On the discovery side, I should also note that we need to be careful about how we frame the arbitration motion — if we move to compel arbitration for only the 312 covered users, plaintiffs' counsel may try to use that to argue the class should proceed as to the remaining 168, or seek to challenge the consistency of our position. I'd suggest we think through whether we want to pursue arbitration for the covered subset while simultaneously addressing the uncovered 168 through the injunction approach Marisol mentioned. I don't have additional case information beyond what I've just shared, but I'm happy to dig deeper into any specific discovery questions as we develop the strategy.

transcript.text: I have an important business-side update from this week's business review with the client. The client has confirmed that they will keep the automated referral feature available — they are not disabling the referral functionality itself. However, they will withdraw all referral-related marketing claims and complete that withdrawal within exactly 60 days, without admitting wrongdoing. This aligns closely with the company's proposed limited injunction approach rather than disabling the referral feature. I should note that the client has not yet put this position into the litigation strategy memo, so we should make sure it's formally documented as we finalize our strategy.
